liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (5 reviews): Reviewer ranks the Dark Star>Saint Stephen>The Eleven sequence among the greatest versions they have heard; Reviewer praises the memorable riffs in this Dark Star, calling them as if etched in stone [6][8][13][15][16]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (3 reviews): Lovelight runs over thirty minutes, with very high energy and plenty of crowd hoots and hollers; Pigpen is especially energetic on Lovelight, closing the Stephen>Eleven>Lovelight medley [7][9][13]
- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): Early-set Morning Dew is called one of the best 1969 versions; Reviewer calls Morning Dew really good [9][12][14]
- **Me and My Uncle** (1 review): Bob shows notable vulnerability on Me and My Uncle [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd69-05-23 t01 Hard To Handle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **gd69-05-23 t02 Morning Dew**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **gd69-05-23 t03 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **gd69-05-23 t04 Dark Star**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **gd69-05-23 t05 St. Stephen**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **gd69-05-23 t06 The Eleven**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **gd69-05-23 t07 Turn On Your Lovelight**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-05-23.141038.sbd.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 91 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd69-05-23.sbd.kaplan.12223.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 87 min; rated 4.29/5 by 17 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard recording great; Described as a spectacular-sounding copy and a sonic upgrade over the older tape; Good quality overall, but a source change in The Eleven mars it [2][6][9][10][12]
- **gd1969-05-23.sbd.gmb.96631.flac16**: soundboard; 6 songs; 43 min; rated 2.4/5 by 5 [4]
- **gd1969-05-23.179026.sbd.daniel.flac1644**: soundboard; 7 songs; 87 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer imagines the show happening out in the middle of nowhere in South Florida [16]
- Billed as the Big Rock Pow Wow, with Johnny Winter, Sweetwater, Muddy Waters, Timothy Leary, NRBQ and others [1]
- Includes a brief intro before Hard To Handle and seconds at the end where the emcee says the band will return [1]
- Reviewer finds the Dark Star>St. Stephen>Eleven good but well short of the 4/27/69 version [7]
- Reviewer ranks this Dark Star second only to 2/27/69 (Live Dead), but prefers the Eleven from the 24th [10]
- Much better than the band on 4/21/69 at the Ark in Boston, heard a month earlier [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-05-23.141038.sbd.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Reels > 1st generation reels > 2nd generation reels > PCM (Sony HG beta tape) [1]
- **gd69-05-23.sbd.kaplan.12223.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jim Hale, Seth Kaplan & JCotsman; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Compiled from a reel master and what is believed to be a cassette master; One source came from a Serafin edit, listed as reel but possibly cassette-mastered, per Eaton's list [2]
- **gd1969-05-23.sbd.gmb.96631.flac16**: transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Soundboard Master Reels > PCM > DAT [4]. Also: This copy is missing St. Stephen into Turn On Your Love Light [4]
- **gd1969-05-23.179026.sbd.daniel.flac1644**: transferred by Daniel; source: This is an speed corrected version of shn=141038 [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Seminole Indian Village - May 23, 1969](https://www.dead.net/show/may-23-1969) [22]
